question: how much of the Hecke tower does convention D discard?
answer: Catalan(n)/n! is retained: 83.3 % at n=3 (A=1), 0.043 % at n=12 (A=4). The cost is n-dependent, so the D-canonical and full-tower rulings may both hold in their own domains.
scope: (b) — exact integer combinatorics. Adjudicates neither ruling.

assertions.name: burnside_check_sum_of_squares_is_n_factorial
assertions.detail: sum_lambda (f^lambda)^2 = n! at every n in {3,6,9,12,15,18}, so the hook-length dimensions are right before anything is concluded from them.

assertions.name: two_row_sector_dimension_is_exactly_catalan
assertions.detail: summing (f^lambda)^2 over the <=2-row partitions gives exactly C(2n,n)/(n+1) at every n checked — i.e. dim TL_n = Catalan(n), verified rather than quoted. This is the dimension convention D retains.

assertions.name: truncation_cost_is_n_dependent_83pct_at_A1_and_0.04pct_at_A4
assertions.detail: n=3 (A=1): 5/6 = 83.3333 %; n=6 (A=2): 132/720 = 18.3333 %; n=9 (A=3): 4,862/362,880 = 1.3398 %; n=12 (A=4): 208,012/479,001,600 = 0.0434 %; n=15 (A=5): 9,694,845/1,307,674,368,000 = 0.0007 %; n=18 (A=6): 477,638,700/6,402,373,705,728,000 = 0.0000 %. So the cost is n-DEPENDENT: the Q_beta ladder is an H_3 object where D discards a single 1-dim block and keeps 83 %, which is why C-vs-D differs only in the 4th decimal on beta_Bor (0.99836662 vs 0.99856216); the mass work is at n = 3A, where ^4He retains 0.043 %.

assertions.name: this_replaces_an_adjective_and_adjudicates_nothing
assertions.detail: the companion PR called the discarded part 'the overwhelming majority of the tower' — an adjective, and not something an owner can rule on. The number says 'D canonical' (2026-08-15) and 'use the full tower' (2026-09-03) may BOTH be right in their own domains, and the live question is where the crossover bites. Measured, not adjudicated.
